_source: 06 sections 2 (Combat Setup) and 3 (Round Order), with the row capacity of section 13 and the surprise die of 01 section 12. Later sections of 06 add their own tables to this file.

surprise._source: 06 section 2 step 3 and 01 section 12. Each side rolls a d6; a side that rolls inside its band surprises the other. Only one side surprised means a round 0 in which only that side acts.

initiative._source: 06 section 3, Initiative. Rolled fresh every round; monsters of the same type share one roll.
initiative._bands: first = under Quicksilver; last = Slowed, plus the Zombie, which always acts last. Both are flags on the unit (actsFirst / actsLast), so a potion, a condition and a monster's own tactics all reach the same band.

turnStartOrder._source: 06 section 4 steps 5-6 and section 5 step 3, which order the start of a turn more finely than section 16's example column: every source of damage, then every source of healing.

damage._source: 06 section 7, with the Res / Weak / Imm line of 02. Every multiplier rounds down where it lands, as 06 section 1 rule 4 says.
damage._overTime: Damage over time and auras (Poisoned, Burning, Bleeding, auras, Molten Shell, Heat Aura, Thorned) skip these steps. Types still matter, so a fire-immune unit ignores Burning.
damage._weaponAttribute: 06 section 7 step 4 and 01 section 8: weapon damage adds the attacker's own modifier — MIG for melee, AGI for a thrown weapon, nothing for a bow or a spell. A monster states its flat in its damage line, so only a unit with attributes adds one.

zeroHp._source: 06 section 9. The traits that catch a unit at 0 HP are hooks; these are the numbers they use.

fallen._source: Troll, Won't Stay Down. The combat does not end while an unburned troll is Fallen.

morale._source: 06 section 9, Morale Triggers. Each trigger fires at most once per monster.

fleeing._source: 06 section 14: d20 + AGI mod + LCK mod vs 10 + the number of living enemies.

attack._source: 06 section 6, and its Attack Modifiers table. Critical range is 01 section 4: a natural 20, or 19-20 with a Luck modifier of +2 or better, which a unit carries as its own critFrom.

turn._source: 06 section 4 (Defend, Hidden, Free Actions) and section 5 step 6 (recharge).

actions._source: 06 section 4. `tags` are what the legality table blocks: a condition that blocks `melee` stops melee attacks and melee skills alike.

telegraph._note: 06 section 5: a monster spends its action announcing the attack.

actions._monsterOnly: 06 sections 11 to 13: what a monster spends its turn on when it is not swinging. None of them is ever offered to the hero.

summon._note: 06 section 13: units arrive in the row the ability names.

heal._note: 02 section 6: the Goblin Shaman mends its kin.

hex._note: 02 section 6: a Mind save, or the hero's next attack goes wide.

guard._note: 02 section 5: the Bone Warden's Tower Shield.

erase._note: 02 section 11: the Grimoire rubs a spell out.

legality._source: 06 section 4, Action Legality. Conditions bring their own `blocks` lists from conditions.json; these are the situations that are not conditions.

noEscape._note: Boss fights, and any monster with preventsFlight (the Frozen Revenant). Smoke Bomb, Vanish and Teleport fail here too.

legality._reasons: Every reason a button can be dimmed for that is not a condition. A condition dims a button under its own name from strings.json.

roundStartOrder._source: 06 section 3 steps 3-5, which is a finer order than the example column of section 16.

reactionFlags._source: 06 section 3 step 2. Reset at the start of every round, for any unit that has them.

_reactions: 06 section 17, Reaction prompts: the Auto setting uses Lucky or Arcane Shield when the hit would take more than 25% of max HP. Until the Phase 8 prompt exists every fight plays Auto; Riposte and Spellblade are spent whenever the hero can pay (docs/DECISIONS.md).
